Change c0179. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. VIII.

Context before (unchanged): The idea of this visit was torture to me, yet I could not refuse.

1818 text: We entered the gloomy prison-chamber, and beheld Justine sitting on some straw at the further end; her hands were manacled, and her head rested on her knees.

1831 text: We entered the gloomy prison-chamber, and beheld Justine sitting on some straw at the farther end; her hands were manacled, and her head rested on her knees.

Diff: We entered the gloomy prison-chamber, and beheld Justine sitting on some straw at the [-further-] {+farther+} end; her hands were manacled, and her head rested on her knees.

Context after (unchanged): She rose on seeing us enter; and when we were left alone with her, she threw herself at the feet of Elizabeth, weeping bitterly.

result.rationale: 'further' becomes 'farther' at the end of the prison chamber. It is a variant-form or usage swap with the same meaning and no interpretive consequence. It is close to orthography, but these are distinct word forms, so wording fits best.
